evidence.evidence_text: Aerial vision-and-language navigation (VLN) — requiring drones to interpret natural language instructions and navigate complex urban environments — emerges as a critical embodied AI challenge that bridges human-robot interaction, 3D spatial reasoning, and real-world deployment.
In this work, we propose CityNavAgent, a large language model (LLM)-empowered agent that significantly reduces the navigation complexity for urban aerial VLN.
In this work, we propose CityNavAgent, a large language model (LLM)-empowered agent that significantly reduces the navigation complexity for urban aerial VLN.

Although existing ground VLN agents achieved notable results in indoor and outdoor settings, they struggle in aerial VLN due to the absence of predefined navigation graphs and the exponentially expanding action space in long-horizon exploration.
Specifically, we design a hierarchical semantic planning module (HSPM) that decomposes the long-horizon task into sub-goals with different semantic levels.
Further experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of different modules of CityNavAgent for aerial VLN in continuous city environments.
